newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open lower, focus on NAPM index.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open lower, focus on NAPM index.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened lower on Tuesday, in line with overseas trends, as the market looked ahead to the mid-morning release of a closely watched measure of activity in the nation's manufacturing sector.
Analysts said the release of the National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) September index was likely to be the pivotal element of the trading sesssion.
The NAPM provides one of the earliest glimpses of economic activity in the month just ended, giving a detailed look at business conditions in the nation's manufacturing sector.
At 0815 EDT/1215 GMT, the 6-3/4 percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond was down 4/32 to 97-22/32, yielding 6.93 percent.
At 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, the Conference Board will release the index of leading economic indicators. Economists at MMS forecast a 0.2 percent rise in the August index.

The MMS economists said all three of the durables-related items will subtract from the index, as will building permits. Sensitive prices, stock prices and unemployment claims will boost the index, they said.
At 0900 EDT/1300 GMT, the BTM/Schroder's index of chain store sales is rumored to show a decline for the latest week.

"There was a little selling overnight in the short- to intermediate- coupons related to swaps," said Josh Stiles, senior bond strategist at I.D.E.A. "The market is a little jittery about NAPM. They will be looking especially at prices paid and at delivery times. The general sense in the market is that the headline number will be rather steady, but the components are where the market's sensitivity lies."
But Stiles cited "support underneath the market from the view that the payroll number will be soft."
Because of that, the NAPM "would have to be a disastrous number to get us all the way back to seven percent (on the 30-year bond yield)," said Stiles.
As for the weekly chain store sales indices, analysts noted that the reports have been running soft.
"At some point you should get a rebound there because the consumer is in pretty good shape as far as income, job outlook, and stock prices," said Stiles.
Analysts said the index of leading economic indicators would not be likely to move the market. The index came in at +0.2 percent for August, in line with expectations.
Three- and six-month bill rates were unchanged at 5.01 percent and 5.18 percent, respectively.
Two-year note prices were down 1/32 to 99-25/32, yielding 6.12 percent.
Prices of five-year notes were unchanged at 99-20/32, yielding 6.46 percent.
The Ten-year notes were down 2/32 to 102-1/32, yielding 6.71 percent.
